messages.text: Item surprises big two for Juddmonte International glory

metadata.summary: Item delivered for Andrew Balding and the sponsors to land a 10-1 surprise in the Juddmonte International at York – with the big two of Constitution River and Ombudsman only third and fourth respectively.
metadata.content: Item surprises big two for Juddmonte International glory | Racing News | Sky Sports Skip to content Item surprises big two for Juddmonte International glory We were treated to another epic renewal of the Juddmonte International on Wednesday but it was far from the match-race that it was built up to be, with Item delivered late to deny Almaqam in a thrilling finish to the York feature. Wednesday 19 August 2026 16:30, UK Image: Item ridden by Colin Keane on their way to winning the Juddmonte International Stakes Item delivered for Andrew Balding and the sponsors to land a 10-1 surprise in the Juddmonte International at York – with the big two of Constitution River and Ombudsman only third and fourth respectively. Hawk Mountain rather unexpectedly set the early pace, with stablemate Constitution River tucked in keenly behind him and odds-on favourite Ombudsman at the rear under William Buick, kept company by another Aidan O'Brien runner, Action. Hawk Mountain was still in front as they moved to the top of the long Knavesmire straight, with Buick beginning to make headway on the inside rail, as Ryan Moore and Constitution River kicked for home over two furlongs out. Ombudsman kept making ground on the inside, but the dangers were coming on the outside and it was Ed Walker's Almaqam who pulled away with half a furlong to run, only for Item to arrive in full flight, just getting his head down on the line in the hands of Colin Keane. metadata.content: Ezri Konsa transfer news: Arsenal agree deal with Aston Villa to sign England defender | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to content Transfer Ezri Konsa transfer news: Arsenal agree deal with Aston Villa to sign England defender Ezri Konsa had two years remaining on his Aston Villa contract; Arsenal also held an interest in Jarell Quansah but look set to move for Konsa; Arsenal currently have William Saliba and Jurrien Timber out injured By Adrian Kajumba and Lyall Thomas Wednesday 19 August 2026 16:03, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch Ezri Konsa's best moments for Aston Villa last season Arsenal have agreed a £51m deal to sign Ezri Konsa from Aston Villa. Arsenal are currently looking for a new defender with William Saliba out for an extended period of time, with Jurrien Timber also sidelined with a long-term groin problem. Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Danyal Khan brings the latest on Ezri Konsa, as Arsenal agree a deal with Aston Villa for the defender. If he is not signed in time for Arsenal's opening Premier League game against Coventry on Friday, Konsa's Gunners debut could take place away at Aston Villa, live on Sky Sports' Monday Night Football on August 31. The Gunners' interest in Konsa has lasted all summer with Villa initially valuing him at £60m - a valuation Arsenal were unwilling to meet. messages.text: Sainz signs multi-year contract extension with Williams

metadata.summary: Carlos Sainz has signed a multi-year contract extension with Williams that will keep him with the team for the 2027 Formula 1 season and beyond.
metadata.content: Carlos Sainz: Williams driver signs multi-year contract extension to remain with team for 2027 F1 season and beyond | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to content Carlos Sainz: Williams driver signs multi-year contract extension to remain with team for 2027 F1 season and beyond Carlos Sainz signs multi-year extension with Williams; announcement follows team-mate Alex Albon signing extension a day earlier; watch the Dutch Grand Prix Sprint weekend live on Sky Sports F1 from Friday Wednesday 19 August 2026 15:41, UK Image: Carlos Sainz has signed a multi-year contract extension with Williams Carlos Sainz has signed a multi-year contract extension with Williams that will keep him with the team for the 2027 Formula 1 season and beyond. The 31-year-old Spaniard had expressed doubt over his future with Williams amid a second campaign with the team that has failed to deliver the strong results of 2025, which makes his decision to sign a multi-year deal something of a surprise. Wednesday's announcement came a day after the team confirmed Sainz's team-mate Alex Albon had signed a one-year extension to remain with the team for the 2027 season, with both drivers' previous deals having been set to expire at the end of 2026.
